What ended the 41 capped turns in the phase 033 untuned arm, and can a runtime-keyed wall-clock cap reduce them without changing the measured outcome?
What does one brief cost in bytes and tokens on the built state, and which remaining byte is removable without losing the offer contract?
Does the pre-model hook and brief cost consume a measurable share of a behaviour-runner turn's wall clock, so that it competes with the turn cap?
Which latency instrument reports the built state's true p95, and which path does it still miss (cold first prompt, in-process plugin, Codex adapter)?

keyFindings.text: **No byte remains removable from a brief without reversing a swept decision.** The head and companion already share one 320-character budget; the constant block is the comment-hygiene hard block that segment one and the repo's own directive decided to keep. Any further cut would remove offer content or the hard block, not slack. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/render.ts:127] [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/009-ux-performance-cross-cli-research/research/research.md:127]

**No measured hook path exceeded the Claude 2,500 ms budget, but the worst row used 88.7 percent of it.** The maximum 2,218 ms leaves 282 ms of headroom against the Claude hook budget; three rows sit above 2,000 ms. The Codex adapter's 2,800 ms budget and Devin/Cursor's 10 s budgets are farther away. [SOURCE: $TMPDIR/speckit-skill-advisor-metrics/*.jsonl] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/user-prompt-submit.ts:21]

**One brief costs 270.7 bytes on average and 361 bytes at most over 1,138 emitting rows on the built state.** That is about 68 tokens at the renderer's own four-characters-per-token estimate. The variable part is capped at 80 tokens (320 characters) by default, and the constant directive block is appended after that cap, so the 219-byte hygiene directive is about 81 percent of a mean brief. [SOURCE: $TMPDIR/speckit-skill-advisor-metrics/*.jsonl] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/render.ts:104] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/render.ts:620-624]

**Per-day medians move little; the tail moved.** 2026-11-13: n 6,438, p50 193, p95 290, p99 298, max 922. 2026-11-14: n 5,501, p50 196, p95 291, p99 299, max 1,205. 2026-11-15: n 5,256, p50 185, p95 291, p99 344, max 2,218. 2026-11-16 (partial): n 580, p50 136, p95 212, p99 308, max 2,208. The p95 is flat across three days while the max tripled. [SOURCE: $TMPDIR/speckit-skill-advisor-metrics/*.jsonl]

**The 300 ms boundary is instrumented on the shim side, and the mechanism is unconfirmed.** The Claude shim reserves `CHILD_START_MARGIN_MS = 300` "after advisor CLI", and the hook stamps `durationMs` from its own start to the brief result. Which component stops at 300 ms is not proven by the record alone; a trace of one prompt whose duration crosses the boundary is what would confirm it. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/user-prompt-submit.ts:21-22] [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/skill-advisor/claude/user-prompt-submit.ts:383]

**The arena arm ran at an earlier commit than the dispatch brief's HEAD.** The five arenas were built at `b765c7a14c5`; HEAD is `84de3d600fa`, six commits later, all documentation and review commits. The arm's behaviour numbers are therefore evidence about `b765c7a14c5`, and no code that affects hook time changed between the two commits. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/033-untuned-arm-arena-run/scratch/arenas.txt:1] [SOURCE: `git log --format='%h %ad %s'` at HEAD sequence 84de3d600fa, b765c7a14c5]

**The built state's hook cost is p50 189 ms, p95 290 ms, p99 300 ms, max 2,218 ms over 17,775 persisted records.** Records run 2026-11-13 to 2026-11-16 and include the phase 033 arena's own prompts. Seven rows exceed 1,000 ms and three exceed 2,000 ms. [SOURCE: $TMPDIR/speckit-skill-advisor-metrics/*.jsonl] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/metrics.ts:402]

**The cap is keyed to the prompt, not the runtime, and the runner records no turn duration.** `CAP_MS` is 300,000 ms for a chat turn and 900,000 ms for a started one, chosen by `G2_PROMPTS.has(rowId)`. `spawnTurn` passes `timeout: capMs` and settles only `{exit}`, and the run line stores `exit` alone, so a null exit conflates a cap kill with a spawn error. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/routing-accuracy/run-command-behaviour.mjs:78-81] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/routing-accuracy/run-command-behaviour.mjs:965] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/routing-accuracy/run-command-behaviour.mjs:1063-1095]

**The capped turns' wall time cannot be recovered from the OpenCode store today.** None of the five local OpenCode databases holds a phase 033 arena session id, and the active store holds zero sessions for the arena directory, so no message timestamp survives to measure how long a capped turn actually ran. [SOURCE: read-only count queries against ~/.local/share/opencode/{opencode.db,opencode-v1.db,opencode-v2.db,opencode-rerun.db,opencode-shots.db}] [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/033-untuned-arm-arena-run/scratch/runs/opencode.jsonl]

**The committed arm's capped-turn count is 47, not the 41 in the dispatch brief.** `summary-arm.json` counts opencode 26 (15 off, 11 on), devin 19 (10 off, 9 on), pi 2 (off), claude 0 and dsh 0 across 400 runs. The raw exit census agrees except for one row: 28 runs exited 143 (opencode 26, pi 2) and 20 exited null (devin), of which one null is the documented `fresh-skill-04` rebase row rather than a cap. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/033-untuned-arm-arena-run/scratch/summary-arm.json] [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/033-untuned-arm-arena-run/scratch/runs/opencode.jsonl]

**The duration distribution has a hard cliff at 300 ms, so p95 290 ms measures a deadline, not the work.** 4,674 of 17,775 rows (26.3 percent) are spread almost uniformly across 240-299 ms, about 778 per 10 ms bin, while only 87 rows (0.49 percent) land beyond 300 ms (81 in 300-309 ms, 6 at 310 ms or more). A uniform plateau followed by a cliff is a wait being cut, not a workload distribution. [SOURCE: $TMPDIR/speckit-skill-advisor-metrics/*.jsonl] [INFERENCE: based on the 240-299 ms plateau and the 300 ms start-margin constant beside the hook's child timeout]

**A capped OpenCode turn was still producing messages 7 seconds before it was killed.** The sampled `opencode fresh-fit-02` session runs 02:07:12 to 02:12:05 (293 s) across 142 records and its run line exits 143; `opencode fresh-fit-03`, uncapped, runs 291 s and exits 0. The cut lands on active work, not on an idle process, for at least that row. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/033-untuned-arm-arena-run/scratch/step-reader/sessions/opencode-fresh-fit-02.json] [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/033-untuned-arm-arena-run/scratch/runs/opencode.jsonl]

**A runtime-keyed cap is the wrong lever; a behaviour-keyed cap is the targeted one.** Claude and DSH capped 0 of 80 fresh runs each, so a runtime key would give them nothing. OpenCode and Devin carried all 48 caps. What would remove them is giving a turn the 900 s cap once it opens a workflow, not because of which runtime carried it. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/033-untuned-arm-arena-run/scratch/runs/claude.jsonl] [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/033-untuned-arm-arena-run/scratch/runs/dsh.jsonl]

**Every capped turn sits in the 300 s group; not one 900 s row was cut.** All 48 raw cap exits are `fresh-*` rows: opencode 26, devin 20 (19 counted plus the restore-failed `fresh-skill-04` null), pi 2, claude 0, dsh 0. The six `g2-*` rows, which get 900 s, were never capped. The 47-count in the committed summary and the 48 raw exits differ only by that restore-failed row. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/033-untuned-arm-arena-run/scratch/runs/opencode.jsonl] [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/033-untuned-arm-arena-run/scratch/runs/devin.jsonl] [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/033-untuned-arm-arena-run/scratch/summary-arm.json]

**Hook cost is not a measurable share of a turn's wall clock.** The built-state hook p95 of 290 ms is 1.9 percent of the shortest sampled turn (15 s) and 0.10 percent of a 298 s turn; at the p50 of 189 ms the share is 0.06-1.3 percent. Even the 2,218 ms worst row is 0.7 percent of a 300 s turn. [SOURCE: $TMPDIR/speckit-skill-advisor-metrics/*.jsonl] [INFERENCE: based on hook percentiles from iteration 1 and the sampled turn durations in this iteration]

**Successful turns stack against the 300 s boundary, so the cap slices a live tail rather than a hang.** The 20 sampled sessions run 15, 24, 25, 41, 44, 61, 63, 72, 79, 90, 104, 167, 291, 293, 293, 298 s (DSH 64, 240, 262, 298 s). Four sampled successes finish within 10 s of the cap, on three runtimes. A cap that were 2.5x a typical turn would not have four of twenty completions inside its last 10 seconds. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/033-untuned-arm-arena-run/scratch/step-reader/sessions/] [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/033-untuned-arm-arena-run/scratch/step-reader/pick.txt]

**The cap is keyed to row-set membership, not to what the turn did.** `capForRow` returns 900,000 ms only when the row id is in `G2_PROMPTS`; every other row gets 300,000 ms. The `fresh-*` rows include prompts that launch a writing workflow (`/create:goal`, `/create:command`), yet they are capped as chat turns. So the runner's own comment that "a started workflow legitimately needs the longer one" is true only for the six rows it already knows are started. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/routing-accuracy/run-command-behaviour.mjs:78-81] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/routing-accuracy/run-command-behaviour.mjs:965] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/routing-accuracy/run-command-behaviour.mjs:846-884]

**The cap's cost is measurable in lost judgeable rows, not in wall time saved.** 26 of 80 OpenCode fresh runs (32.5 percent) and 20 of 81 Devin fresh runs (24.7 percent) ended capped, against 0 of 80 on Claude and DSH. Those are the rows the summary already excludes from "judgeable offers", so the cap decides how much of the arm can be scored at all. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/033-untuned-arm-arena-run/scratch/summary-arm.json]

[SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/metrics.ts:482-492]

[SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/003-plain-chat-command-reach/scratch/hook-latency-before.json] [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/004-command-meaning-matching/scratch/hook-latency-after-3.json] [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/005-recommendation-contract-and-brief/scratch/hook-latency-after-3.json]

**Per-runtime live p95 is 308 ms on Claude, 279 on DSH, 264 on Pi, 237 on Devin and 742 on Vibe.** Codex has six live rows at p95 161 ms, too few to read. Vibe is the only runtime whose p95 exceeds Claude's, and it is also the one with the smallest live sample (49 rows). [SOURCE: $TMPDIR/speckit-skill-advisor-metrics/*.jsonl]

**The built-state brief median is 262 bytes, 44 bytes below segment four's 306-byte median on typed rows.** The populations differ (organic prompts versus 44 typed rows), so this is consistent with, not proof of, the phase 021 head change trimming the head. What would confirm it: the same 44 typed rows re-measured on the built state. [SOURCE: $TMPDIR/speckit-skill-advisor-metrics/*.jsonl] [INFERENCE: based on the 262-byte built-state median and segment four's 306-byte typed-row median] [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/009-ux-performance-cross-cli-research/research/research-segment-4.md:167]

**The organic record has two modes, and the median describes the cheap one.** Of 1,695 live rows, 980 (57.8 percent) are cache hits; Claude's live median is 30 ms while its live p95 is 308 ms. The fixed probe never observes a cache hit, so a probe median of ~200 ms and an organic median of 30 ms are both true and describe different paths. [SOURCE: $TMPDIR/speckit-skill-advisor-metrics/*.jsonl]

**Both cold waits on the server side are twice the caller's budget.** The CLI waits up to 5,000 ms for a cold daemon (`COLD_START_WAIT_MS`), and the local scorer has a 5,000 ms deadline (`LOCAL_SCORER_TIMEOUT_MS`); the hook that called them gives up at 2,500 ms. A path that honours its own 5 s wait can only ever be observed from the caller as a timeout. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/skill-advisor-cli.ts:33-36] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/skill-advisor-cli.ts:43-45]

**The cascade probe's default 2,500 ms can consume the whole hook child budget before any scoring work starts.** `SPECKIT_CASCADE_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS` defaults to 2,500 ms inside `auto-select.ts`, while the Claude shim kills its child at 2,500 ms. A probe that runs to its default therefore leaves zero time for the CLI, and the failure mode is a fail-open brief, not a slow brief. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/shared/embeddings/auto-select.ts:116-119] [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/skill-advisor/claude/user-prompt-submit.ts:160]

**The measured cold work is about 690 ms: 271-277 ms for a cold embedding call plus 413 ms for the advisor CLI with the model cold.** Against the 2,500 ms Claude hook budget that is 27.6 percent, so a cold first prompt does not by itself exhaust the budget. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/008-embedder-setup-and-cost/spec.md:132]

**The production record prices the cold failure at zero.** The 664 `unavailable` rows have p50 0 ms and p95 2 ms, so a cold first prompt that fails open contributes the cheapest possible row to every aggregate; the population that should carry the cold cost carries none of it. [SOURCE: $TMPDIR/speckit-skill-advisor-metrics/*.jsonl]

**What would confirm the bound: one sandbox cold start with the model unloaded.** Unload the embed model, wait past its five-minute keep-alive, run one prompt through the real hook and record wall time, the cascade probe's own duration and the fail-open reason. Absent that, 690 ms is measured work and 2,500 ms is a waiting bound, not a first-prompt cost. [INFERENCE: based on findings 1-4]

**A long-lived operator session would amortize toward a 26-90 byte head, but no row set here measures that share.** The head is a single line (median 88 bytes in segment four) and the directive is 219 bytes, so a reduced delivery would land in the 26-90 byte range depending on the head's command and score decoration. What would confirm the amortized figure: five or more prompts sharing one session id with a growing transcript, recording `emittedBytes` per prompt. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/009-ux-performance-cross-cli-research/research/research-segment-4.md:167] [INFERENCE: based on the head and directive byte split]

**Brief bytes are tightly clustered and almost never head-only.** p10 244, p25 260, p50 262, p75 286, p90 298, max 361 bytes. Only 9 of 1,234 briefs (0.7 percent) fall below 120 bytes, the size a head-only delivery would have; 1,221 (99.0 percent) are at or above 240 bytes. [SOURCE: $TMPDIR/speckit-skill-advisor-metrics/*.jsonl]

**In an arm where every turn is a new session, the dedup cannot fire, so 270.6 bytes is the per-prompt cost, not an upper bound.** The behaviour runner starts each row as its own runtime session, and the measured population agrees: 99 percent of briefs carry the full block. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/hooks/lib/directive-lifecycle.ts:129-137] [INFERENCE: based on the dedup gate's session requirement and the 0.7 percent head-only share]

**The dedup gate needs a proven continuing session, so a fresh turn always pays the directive.** Reduced delivery requires a non-empty confirmed session id, a valid transcript with byte size, a stable state clock across two reads, and a transcript that has not shrunk; a new session, a lifecycle boundary, a changed directive set or a shrunk transcript all force the full block. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/hooks/lib/directive-lifecycle.ts:121-179]

**A Claude prompt runs five Node processes, and the advisor record times three of them.** `.claude/settings.json` declares three `UserPromptSubmit` commands — the spec-kit shim, `spec-gate-classify.mjs` and `context-nudge.mjs` — each with `timeout: 3`. The shim then spawns the advisor hook, which spawns the advisor CLI, so the advisor path alone is three starts and the prompt pays two more hooks outside that path. [SOURCE: .claude/settings.json] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/user-prompt-submit.ts:21-22]

**At the committed 36.85 ms bare-Node start, the advisor's three starts are about 111 ms, or 64 percent of the uncached median.** Collapsing the CLI spawn and the adapter spawn would recover about 74 ms, 43 percent of the uncached p50. Both figures are estimates built on a start cost measured on this machine in an earlier segment, not on the built state. [INFERENCE: based on 3 × 36.85 ms against the 172 ms uncached p50] [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/009-ux-performance-cross-cli-research/research/research.md:78]

**Claude's uncached live path is p50 172 ms, p90 348, p95 618, max 1,538 ms over 529 rows.** The cached path is p50 30, p95 151, max 913 over 926 rows. The 2,500 ms budget holds at 4x the uncached p95. [SOURCE: $TMPDIR/speckit-skill-advisor-metrics/*.jsonl]

**The health record cannot price the whole prompt, because two of the three hook commands are outside it.** The advisor's `durationMs` covers its own leg; `spec-gate-classify` and `context-nudge` have no join to it, so a prompt's total hook latency is at least the advisor leg plus two more Node starts that no single record sums. [SOURCE: .claude/settings.json] [INFERENCE: based on three independent UserPromptSubmit commands and the advisor record's own start and end stamps]

**What would confirm the ceiling: one timing probe that runs the three configured hooks in the host's order.** Record wall time per command and total, then compare with the advisor leg alone. Absent that, 111 ms and 74 ms are ceilings, not savings. [INFERENCE: based on findings 2 and 3]

**No measured cell in this ledger exceeds a runtime's budget.** The worst live p95 is Claude's uncached 618 ms against 2,500 ms (24.7 percent); the worst single live row is 1,538 ms (61.5 percent); the cold chain's measured work is 690 ms and its risk is the 2,500 ms probe ceiling, not the model. [SOURCE: $TMPDIR/speckit-skill-advisor-metrics/*.jsonl] [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/skill-advisor/claude/user-prompt-submit.ts:160]

**The brief costs about 68 tokens per prompt in a fresh-session population.** 270.6 bytes mean, 262 median, 316 p95 at the renderer's four-characters-per-token estimate; 99 percent of briefs carry the full 219-byte directive. [SOURCE: $TMPDIR/speckit-skill-advisor-metrics/*.jsonl] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/render.ts:104-127]
